page: Microsoft Azure E32ps_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the Epsv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores powered by the Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor architecture operating at 3.4 GHz, with one thread per core. The memory configuration consists of 256.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high resource density of 8.0 GB per core. There is no integrated local storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance, though it is compatible with Premium Storage.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core capabilities and exceptional memory performance. The server achieved top-tier ratings in memory bandwidth, with read-only large block speeds of 436.06 GB/sec and write large block speeds of 184.19 GB/sec. Passmark database operations also placed in the top tier at 37,163.36 operations. Multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core tests registered as strong. However, single-core performance on stress-ng and Geekbench remains in the average tier, and the lack of AVX or AMX instruction sets limits specialized vector math.

The qualitative cost efficiency of this server is driven by its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and the power efficiency of the ARM64 architecture, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads without the premium cost of x86 equivalents. Tradeoffs include the absence of local NVMe storage and poor performance in large-scale AI workloads, as evidenced by a poor rating of 4.66 tokens/sec for 70B LLM prompt processing. This server is best suited for relational databases, in-memory caching, data processing pipelines, and web serving workloads that benefit from high memory bandwidth and dedicated physical cores.
